claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside it inherit the package's version.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository and its version is the Git tag on that repository.

Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow: apply a semver Git tag, then run `pulumi package publish` to send package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and place it in the Private Registry.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry; source-based packages referenced directly from a Pulumi.yaml can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit).

Executable-based plugin packages are distributed as pre-built plugin binaries, typically with per-language SDKs published to feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, Go module proxy); the package version is the version embedded in the binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can publish executable-based packages to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
Pulumi recommends a repository contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components to secure and operate it.
A single PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.
Bundling unrelated components in one package causes every release to version every component the same way, violating semver; Pulumi does not recommend a single monorepo with one giant package.
Links target pages exist: /docs/idp/concepts/private-registry/, /docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_package_publish/, packaging-components anchors, and publishing-packages guide.
